# R programming for beginners. Manipulate data using the tidyverse: select, filter and mutate.

<https://youtu.be/nRtp7wSEtJA?si=gYTjwzAubesA5gja>

```{r}
install.packages("tidyverse") #do it once
library(tidyverse) #or use require()

```

```{r}
#to see dataset available in R
data()
#lets use starwars
View(starwars)
```

Now we are going to try to get the BMI of humans in this dataset. to see the name of the variables

```{r}
names(starwars)

```

```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species)
```

we want human only

```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit()#to remove the missing value
```

lets change the height to metre

```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(height = height/100)
```

now lets create a new variable= BMI

```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(height = height/100) %>% 
  mutate(BMI = mass/height^2)
  
```

is there a difference between BMI of male and female? lets find out

```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(height = height/100) %>% 
  mutate(BMI = mass/height^2) %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% 
  summarise(Average_BMI = mean(BMI))
```

# 10 data filtering tips using R programming. Use the tidyverse to filter and subset your data.

https://youtu.be/pU10ghMvAuM?si=07lIKgMAJH6IbRXX

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
View(msleep)
names(msleep)
```
Lets talk about ways to use filter function in R

```{r}
my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(sleep_total > 18)
my_data
```
the next way is to use the '!' , which means 'not'

```{r}
my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(!sleep_total > 18)
my_data
```

what if we want to filter more than 1 criteria? we use the ',' to indicate the boolean operator of AND

```{r}
my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, order, bodywt, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(order == "Primates", bodywt > 20)
my_data
```
the next thing we can do it using the boolean operator OR rather than AND

```{r}
my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, order, bodywt, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(order == "Primates"| bodywt > 20)
my_data
```
we can also use the OR operator multiple times

```{r}
msleep$name

my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(name =="Cow"|
           name == "Dog" |
           name == "Goat")
my_data
```

slighyly elegant way of doing it
```{r}

my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(name %in% c("Cow", "Dog", "Horse"))
my_data
```
also in filter, we can use between

```{r}

my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(between(sleep_total, 16, 18))
my_data
```

now we are filter out value with near to our specified number

```{r}

my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(near(sleep_total, 17, tol = 0.5))
my_data
```
and now lets filter those with missing values

```{r}

my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, conservation, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(is.na(conservation))
my_data
```

and the opposite of the above, we wanted to filter those not missing. guess what, just use '!'

```{r}
my_data <- msleep %>% 
  select(name, conservation, sleep_total) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(conservation))
my_data
```

#Group by and summarise

```{r}
require(tidyverse)
```
```{r}
view(msleep) #use this dataset, mammal sleep
names(msleep)
```

```{r}
msleep %>% 
  drop_na(sleep_rem, vore) %>% 
  group_by(vore) %>% 
  summarise('Average total sleep' = mean(sleep_total),
            'Maximum rem sleep' = max(sleep_rem)) %>% 
  view
```

```

Lets start

```{r}

glimpse(starwars)#same kind like str, but better
View(starwars)#if you want  to see the dataset, but you can actually click on the environment icon

Beware that NA, none, unknwon might mean differently

```{r}

```

```

```

#Data Cleaning
https://youtu.be/sV5lwAJ7vnQ?si=6Viaj-Ea1Qm2Gk5F

What is clean data?
1. correct variable types
2. select and filter (what you want and dont)
3. find and deal with missing data
4. find and deal with duplicates
5. recoding values


Just like before

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
View(starwars)
glimpse(starwars) #you can see that there is no factor here aka categorical variables
class(starwars$gender) #this variable is a categorical but percieved as character in R
unique(starwars$gender)

```
##Correcting/changing variable types
how to change character variable to factor variable?

```{r}
starwars$gender <- as.factor(starwars$gender)
class(starwars$gender)#to see the change

```
sometimes, a factor variable has level on it, thats make it different from character variable

to see levels
```{r}
levels(starwars$gender)
```
let say we want to change the level, how to do it?

```{r}
starwars$gender <- factor((starwars$gender),
                          levels = c("masculine",
                                     "feminine"))
levels(starwars$gender) # already changed!
```
## Variable Selection
Moving on to the next, to select variables

```{r}
names(starwars)
```

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name,height, ends_with("color")) %>% #select any variable with the names color at the end
  names() #to see the variables right now
```
if you want to see the dataset, just remove the function names
```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name,height, ends_with("color"))
```

if we take hair color, and we want to see the possible observation

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name,height, ends_with("color")) %>% 
  filter(hair_color %in% c("blond", "brown") & #observe the boolean opeartor in action
           height<180)
```

##Missing data
```{r}
mean(starwars$height)
mean(starwars$height, na.rm = T) #if we want to take average properly, need to remove the NA

```
not recommended to do this where you just omit all NA
```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name, gender, hair_color, height) %>% 
  na.omit()
```


to filter for only complete observation of the dataset

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name, gender, hair_color, height) %>% 
  filter(complete.cases(.))
```

want to do the reverse? maybe you want to see what data is missing? here's how.
and now you can get some sense of the missingness 
```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name, gender, hair_color, height) %>% 
  filter(!complete.cases(.))
```

for android like C3PO, of course it dont have hair, so its not really missing, but no hair. might need to replace this

and now for height we might decide on removing those with no documented height

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name, gender, hair_color, height) %>% 
  filter(!complete.cases(.)) %>% 
  drop_na(height)
```

let say we remove the line of !complete.cases

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name, gender, hair_color, height) %>% 
  drop_na(height) %>% 
  View()
```

if we want to replace NA with something else

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name, gender, hair_color, height) %>% 
  filter(!complete.cases(.)) |> 
  mutate(hair_color= replace_na(hair_color, "none"))
```

if we dont overwrite the original variable
```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name, gender, hair_color, height) %>% 
  filter(!complete.cases(.)) |> 
  mutate(hair_color2= replace_na(hair_color, "none"))
```
```
